title: Finite spectral-sum form of the actual Q3 Kubo-Mori generator pairing
question: Can the actual finite Q3 Kubo-Mori generator pairing be written as a nonnegative finite spectral sum over energy gaps, so that the remaining common-alpha obligation is isolated as a uniform control of that spectral second moment rather than another termwise cancellation?

model.graph: registered edge, square, and six-site 2x3 Q3 graphs
model.history: D_sigma(t)=U_(H+sigma W_L)(t) A_2 U_(H+sigma W_L)(t)^* - U_H(t) A_2 U_H(t)^*
model.spectral_pairing: <delta_H^2 D,D>_KM=-2 sum_ij L(p_i,p_j) (E_i-E_j)^2 |D_hat_ij|^2/hbar^2 and <delta_H D,delta_H D>_KM is the opposite nonnegative sum
model.interpretation: The finite spectral second moment is identified exactly; uniform source/volume/beta control of it is not assumed.

adversarial_review.check: The primary commutator lane and independent eigenbasis lane both use delta_H=i[H,·]/hbar and compare the complete signed pairing with the positive spectral sum.
Every sum is over a finite H eigenbasis; no interchange with a volume, cutoff, beta, or continuum limit is made.
The equal-probability logarithmic-mean limit is explicit and the weights are built from the actual finite H Gibbs spectrum.
The spectral second moment is the identified missing quantity; finite rows do not supply a uniform bound or a vanishing high-energy tail.
R312 formalizes the finite rational sum identity only; matrix diagonalization and unbounded domains remain outside Lean.
Common core, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, and Pre-A remain open.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks the exact finite rational sum identity and positivity fixtures; actual Q3 matrix spectra and all infinite-volume/domain claims remain finite-only.

qft_interface.closed: The direct finite Kubo-Mori derivative norm is exactly the square root of a nonnegative Gibbs-weighted spectral second moment, with cancellation identity as its signed companion.
qft_interface.open: A source/volume/beta-uniform common-core bound for that spectral second moment, high-energy tail control, product/core density, exhaustion independence, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum, and Pre-A.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: This separates the exact finite spectral algebra from the unresolved uniform analytic estimate; it is not a QFT reconstruction.

no_overclaim: The finite spectral-sum identity is exact and reusable. It does not prove that the spectral second moment is uniformly bounded, does not close direct D/delta-D Cauchy, and does not close common alpha, Sector A, Pre-A, or any Clay statement.
